newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Zedillo, Chicago's Daley praise free trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Zedillo, Chicago's Daley praise free trade.

text.p: Mexico's President Ernesto Zedillo and the mayor of Chicago, Richard Daley, praised the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) on Thursday, calling the pact a success for Mexico and the United States.

Zedillo and Daley met in the Mexican president's official residence, one day after U.S. President Bill Clinton left Mexico after a state visit in which he also praised the trade ties between the two countries.
"NAFTA has united the cultures of the United States and Mexico, which should have been done many years ago," said Daley, according to a Mexican government press release.
"But we are very proud of the benefits that we have received in the United States, as well as those that Mexico has received," Daley said.
A free trade pact, aimed at lowering trade barriers between Mexico, the United States and Canada, went into effect in 1994.
